sources: Maestro's first drafts, from the theory core's notes (PLAN.md tasks 2.2 to 2.5)
Tempo: DadCraft, Oct 24 (Checkpoint 2); outrun's drive at 112 (task 3.4b)

DadCraft's production notes (docs/taste.md, Oct 23): the bass carrying the groove three ways, high sparkle arps and cold 8th arps, supersaw pads, minor for urgency, fast tracks full from the first beat

Task 3.4b (Oct 24): DadCraft chose outrun as the core with dreamy calm sections, and light pumping; the patterns and sounds are what's widely known of the style (80s polysynths, the LinnDrum and its gated reverb, outrun's octave bass), in our own words

vocabulary.why: Borrowed bVI, bVII and iv; added ninths and sevenths.

leading.why: Pads that glide as a block are fine.

progressions.why: Four-bar loops of a chord a bar, mostly natural minor's own bVI, bIII and bVII (no leading tone: it circles rather than resolves); a bright major loop when a section lifts to a major key. Loops come round as they were, now and then coloured; half the phrases land home.

aeolian loop.why: the classic: home, the chord a semitone over its fifth, the relative major, the step under home

climb home.why: home held, then the two chords that climb back to it

minor four.why: the subdominant first, then the climb

turning.why: rocking between the steps under home

glow.why: for a major key: the bright four-chord loop

sunset.why: for a major key: the same loop from its relative minor, wistful

distance.why: Gentle (DadCraft, Oct 27): calm sections keep to keys and chords that share notes, a Lift may travel a little further; never more than twice as likely.

form.why: Outrun starts at full energy (DadCraft's notes: fast tracks from the first beat); long waves, a key lift a step up.

members.why: Maestro's own sounds (synth.py): a supersaw pad, a saw bass, a plucked arp, a saw lead, a LinnDrum-style kit. The pad and bass duck lightly under the kick (DadCraft, Oct 24: light pumping).

bass.why: The bass carries the groove (DadCraft's notes): octave or root 8ths locked to the kick when the energy is up (outrun), a held sub when it's low (dreamy).

octave eighths.why: outrun's own: the root and its octave in 8ths

rolling sixteenths.why: 16ths on the root, the octave before the bar line

held sub.why: a clean sub under the melody, held through the bar

sub and nudge.why: the held root, struck again on the and of 3

arp.why: A high sparkle arp in 16ths when the energy is up; colder, slower 8ths when it's low (DadCraft's notes). A shape a section, round each chord's tones, an echo on the dotted 8th.

melody.why: A singable lead on top, shaped over the phrase (DadCraft's notes: the melody must stay on top).

drums.why: A drum machine (LinnDrum-style): the snare big on 2 and 4 with its gated reverb, four on the floor or a motorik kick, 8th or 16th hats, open hats on the and; at low energy the kick and snare go half time (the dreamy sections). Tom fills, high to floor, into a new section; a reversed cymbal into some.

patterns.why: Kicks as each bar's 16ths; hats an 8th at a time: - none, x an 8th, xx two 16ths, o an open hat. A kick pattern may set its own snare (half time: on 3).

four on the floor.why: a kick every beat: outrun's drive

push.why: four on the floor, a pickup into the next round

motorik.why: 1 and 3 with the and of 3: forward motion

half time.why: the dreamy sections: the kick on 1, the snare on 3

half time sparse.why: room for the pad to float

bars: x x x x x x x x
x x x x x x x x
xx xx xx xx xx xx xx xx
xx xx xx xx xx xx xx xx
x o x o x o x o
x o x o x o x o
open on the and.why: the open hat on every and

quarters.why: a hat a beat, for air

bars: x x x x x x x x
x x x x x x x o
dreamy eighths.why: 8ths, opening at the end of the round

layers.why: Our own first tendencies (task 3.6), for DadCraft's ear to tune: the pad first, the bass under it, the arp then the drums as the energy rises (after Ouralia's Calm builds); a section rising into a louder one may drop to the arp and pad for its last phrase. Rotation and slow change after Tangerine (research round 6).

judge.why: Written from DadCraft's production notes (docs/taste.md), the Synthwave MIDI Reimaginer's preset (docs/data.md, ideas only) and what's widely known of the style (the LinnDrum's backbeat), not from the entry's patterns.

tempo: docs/taste.md: calm about 60-100, menace 120-140, boss or fanfare 135-170

steps: the drum machine's backbeat on 2 and 4 (Reimaginer: a gated snare); half time in the calm parts (docs/taste.md)
the Reimaginer: four on the floor; docs/taste.md: a motorik pulse

chord tones: docs/taste.md: locked to the kick, or a clean sub under the melody
register: the Reimaginer: the bass around A2

notes: docs/taste.md: a sparkle arp, cold new-wave arps
chord tones: an arp runs round the chord's tones

register: the Reimaginer: the lead centred on G#4 (docs/data.md, an open point)
chord tones: Open Music Theory, "Embellishing tones" (CC BY-SA 4.0): the strong beats take the chord's tones
top: docs/taste.md, "Failures to check for": the melody must stay on top

length: docs/taste.md: supersaw pads stand in for an orchestra; chillwave pads float
voices: docs/taste.md: supersaw chords, sevenths and ninths
